title: What was Instagram worth?
lede: Three of these deals are shown. Two are hidden. Guess the announced price of each hidden deal before you reveal it.
intent: Learners can place an acquisition price in context, and explain why an announced price is not the same as the value paid or the value gained.
goal: place an acquisition price in context, and explain why the announced price is not the whole story.
question: How much did Facebook announce it would pay for Instagram in 2012, and for WhatsApp in 2014?

reveal.heading: A price is only readable next to other prices
reveal.explanation: Instagram was announced at about US$1 billion, less than YouTube six years earlier, for a company with 13 staff and no revenue. Two years later WhatsApp was announced at nineteen times that. And Tumblr, bought for almost exactly Instagram's price, went the other way entirely.
points: Announced prices are headlines. The Instagram deal was mostly Facebook shares, which fell after Facebook's float, so it was worth about US$715 million by the time it closed.
WhatsApp went the opposite way: US$19 billion announced, about US$22 billion by the close.
Yahoo later wrote off most of what it paid for Tumblr, and it was reportedly sold in 2019 for about US$3 million. Same price as Instagram, opposite outcome.

teach.watchFor: Learners concluding that Facebook was obviously clever. Put Tumblr beside Instagram: same price, opposite result. It was a bet, and at the time it looked like one.
ask: Who guessed highest for Instagram? What were you assuming?
Why would a company pay anything for a business with no revenue?
